label: Liu et al. reported position-dependent retrieval in long inputs
summary: Liu and colleagues report that models evaluated on multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval often performed best when relevant information occurred at the start or end of a long input, with marked degradation for middle positions.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

label: RULER expands needle retrieval to multi-hop and aggregation
summary: The RULER paper describes a configurable synthetic long-context benchmark extending needle-in-a-haystack retrieval with different needle types and counts, plus multi-hop tracing and aggregation; it evaluates 17 language models on 13 representative tasks.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

label: RULER performance gap at claimed 32K context
summary: In the RULER authors’ evaluation of 17 long-context models advertised for at least 32K tokens, almost all declined on RULER as input length grew, and the authors reported only about half maintained satisfactory performance at 32K, despite nearly perfect results on vanilla needle retrieval.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

label: NoLiMa tests retrieval without literal matching
summary: The NoLiMa authors introduce a needle-retrieval benchmark in which questions and relevant text have minimal lexical overlap, requiring latent associations rather than straightforward literal matching to locate evidence.

sources.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching

label: NoLiMa reported degradation in 13-model evaluation at 32K
summary: In NoLiMa evaluations of 13 models claiming at least 128K-token support, 11 performed at under half their short-context baseline at 32K; the reported GPT-4o score dropped from 99.3% at short context to 69.7% at 32K.

sources.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching

label: LongBench v2 realistic long-context question collection
summary: The LongBench v2 authors describe 503 multiple-choice questions with source contexts from 8,000 to 2 million words spanning six categories, including multi-document questions and code-repository understanding.

sources.title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks

label: LongBench v2 reported expert and model benchmark accuracies
summary: The LongBench v2 authors report 53.7% human-expert accuracy with a 15-minute limit, 50.1% for the strongest directly answering model, and 57.7% for o1-preview using longer reasoning under their reported evaluation.

sources.title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks

label: BABILong distributes reasoning facts through long documents
summary: BABILong introduces 20 tasks involving fact chaining, induction, deduction, counting and lists or sets, designed to require reasoning over facts distributed through very long natural-language documents.

sources.title: BABILong: Testing the Limits of LLMs with Long Context Reasoning-in-a-Haystack

label: HELMET reported poor predictive validity of simple needle tests
summary: In a study of 59 long-context models, the HELMET authors report that synthetic needle-in-a-haystack scores do not reliably predict downstream performance and that their different application-centered task categories have low correlations.

sources.title: HELMET: How to Evaluate Long-Context Language Models Effectively and Thoroughly

label: InfinityBench longer-than-100K-token benchmark design
summary: The 2024 InfinityBench paper describes a benchmark with average data length above 100K tokens and a mix of synthetic and realistic English and Chinese tasks intended to require long-distance dependencies rather than retrieval of isolated passages.

sources.title: ∞Bench: Extending Long Context Evaluation Beyond 100K Tokens

label: Original LongBench multilingual multitask composition
summary: The original LongBench authors report 21 datasets in six task categories in English and Chinese, with average input lengths of 6,711 English words and 13,386 Chinese characters.

sources.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding

label: LongCite sentence-level citation generation workflow
summary: The LongCite authors propose a Coarse-to-Fine pipeline producing long-context question-answer pairs with sentence-level citations and report using its LongCite-45k training data to train LongCite-8B and LongCite-9B.

sources.title: LongCite: Enabling LLMs to Generate Fine-grained Citations in Long-context QA
